paragraphs.text: translated by
1. BRING forth your sacred song ye prudent singers, even as are the thoughts of human beings.
paragraphs.original: मनीषिणः प्र भरध्वं मनीषां यथायथा मतयः सन्ति नृणाम् ।
paragraphs.translit: manīṣiṇaḥ pra bharadhvaṃ manīṣāṃ yathāyathā matayaḥ santi nṛṇām |

paragraphs.text: Let us draw Indra with true deeds anear us: he loves our songs, the Hero, and is potent.
paragraphs.original: इन्द्रं सत्यैरेरयामा कृतेभिः स हि वीरो गिर्वणस्युर्विदानः
paragraphs.translit: indraṃ satyairerayāmā kṛtebhiḥ sa hi vīro girvaṇasyurvidānaḥ

paragraphs.text: 2. The hymn shone brightly from the seat of worship: to the kine came the Bull, the Heifer's Offspring
paragraphs.original: ऋतस्य हि सदसो धीतिरद्यौत्सं गार्ष्टेयो वृषभो गोभिरानट् ।
paragraphs.translit: ṛtasya hi sadaso dhītiradyautsaṃ gārṣṭeyo vṛṣabho gobhirānaṭ |

paragraphs.text: With mighty bellowing hath he arisen, and hath pervaded even the spacious regions.
paragraphs.original: उदतिष्ठत्तविषेणा रवेण महान्ति चित्सं विव्याचा रजांसि
paragraphs.translit: udatiṣṭhattaviṣeṇā raveṇa mahānti citsaṃ vivyācā rajāṃsi

paragraphs.text: 3. Indra knows, verily, how to hear our singing, for he, victorious, made a path for Surya.
paragraphs.original: इन्द्रः किल श्रुत्या अस्य वेद स हि जिष्णुः पथिकृत्सूर्याय ।
paragraphs.translit: indraḥ kila śrutyā asya veda sa hi jiṣṇuḥ pathikṛtsūryāya |

paragraphs.text: He made the Cow, and be became the Sovran of Heaven, primeval, matchless, and unshaken.
paragraphs.original: आन्मेनां कृण्वन्नच्युतो भुवद्गोः पतिर्दिवः सनजा अप्रतीतः
paragraphs.translit: ānmenāṃ kṛṇvannacyuto bhuvadgoḥ patirdivaḥ sanajā apratītaḥ

paragraphs.text: 4. Praised by Angirases, Indra demolished with might the works of the great watery monster
paragraphs.original: इन्द्रो मह्ना महतो अर्णवस्य व्रतामिनादङ्गिरोभिर्गृणानः ।
paragraphs.translit: indro mahnā mahato arṇavasya vratāminādaṅgirobhirgṛṇānaḥ |

paragraphs.text: Full many regions, too, hath he pervaded, and by his truth supported earth's foundation.
paragraphs.original: पुरूणि चिन्नि तताना रजांसि दाधार यो धरुणं सत्यताता
paragraphs.translit: purūṇi cinni tatānā rajāṃsi dādhāra yo dharuṇaṃ satyatātā

paragraphs.text: 5. The counterpart of heaven and earth is Indra: he knoweth all libations, slayeth Susna.
paragraphs.original: इन्द्रो दिवः प्रतिमानं पृथिव्या विश्वा वेद सवना हन्ति शुष्णम् ।
paragraphs.translit: indro divaḥ pratimānaṃ pṛthivyā viśvā veda savanā hanti śuṣṇam |

paragraphs.text: The vast sky with the Sun hath he extended, and, best otpillars, stayed it with a pillar.
paragraphs.original: महीं चिद्द्यामातनोत्सूर्येण चास्कम्भ चित्कम्भनेन स्कभीयान्
paragraphs.translit: mahīṃ ciddyāmātanotsūryeṇa cāskambha citkambhanena skabhīyān

paragraphs.text: 6. The Vrtra-slaver with his bolt felled Vrtra: the magic of the godless, waxen mighty,
paragraphs.original: वज्रेण हि वृत्रहा वृत्रमस्तरदेवस्य शूशुवानस्य मायाः ।
paragraphs.translit: vajreṇa hi vṛtrahā vṛtramastaradevasya śūśuvānasya māyāḥ |

paragraphs.text: Here hast thou, Bold Assailant, boldly conquered. Yea, then thine arms, O Maghavan, were potent.
paragraphs.original: वि धृष्णो अत्र धृषता जघन्थाथाभवो मघवन्बाह्वोजाः
paragraphs.translit: vi dhṛṣṇo atra dhṛṣatā jaghanthāthābhavo maghavanbāhvojāḥ

paragraphs.text: 7. When the Dawns come attendant upon Surya their rays discover wealth of divers colours.
paragraphs.original: सचन्त यदुषसः सूर्येण चित्रामस्य केतवो रामविन्दन् ।
paragraphs.translit: sacanta yaduṣasaḥ sūryeṇa citrāmasya ketavo rāmavindan |

paragraphs.text: The Star of heaven is seen as 'twere approaching: none knoweth aught of it as it departeth.
paragraphs.original: आ यन्नक्षत्रं ददृशे दिवो न पुनर्यतो नकिरद्धा नु वेद
paragraphs.translit: ā yannakṣatraṃ dadṛśe divo na punaryato nakiraddhā nu veda

paragraphs.text: 8. Far have they gone, the first of all these waters, the waters that flowed forth when Indra sent them.
paragraphs.original: दूरं किल प्रथमा जग्मुरासामिन्द्रस्य याः प्रसवे सस्रुरापः ।
paragraphs.translit: dūraṃ kila prathamā jagmurāsāmindrasya yāḥ prasave sasrurāpaḥ |

paragraphs.text: Where is their spring, and where is their foundation? Where now, ye Waters, is your inmost centre?
paragraphs.original: क्व स्विदग्रं क्व बुध्न आसामापो मध्यं क्व वो नूनमन्तः
paragraphs.translit: kva svidagraṃ kva budhna āsāmāpo madhyaṃ kva vo nūnamantaḥ

paragraphs.text: 9. Thou didst free rivers swallowed by the Dragon; and rapidly they set themselves in motion,
paragraphs.original: सृजः सिन्धूँरहिना जग्रसानाँ आदिदेताः प्र विविज्रे जवेन ।
paragraphs.translit: sṛjaḥ sindhūm̐rahinā jagrasānām̐ ādidetāḥ pra vivijre javena |

paragraphs.text: Those that were loosed and those that longed for freedom. Excited now to speed they run unresting.
paragraphs.original: मुमुक्षमाणा उत या मुमुच्रेऽधेदेता न रमन्ते नितिक्ताः
paragraphs.translit: mumukṣamāṇā uta yā mumucre'dhedetā na ramante nitiktāḥ

paragraphs.text: 10. Yearning together they have sped to Sindhu: the Fort-destroyer, praised, of old, hath loved them.
paragraphs.original: सध्रीचीः सिन्धुमुशतीरिवायन्सनाज्जार आरितः पूर्भिदासाम् ।
paragraphs.translit: sadhrīcīḥ sindhumuśatīrivāyansanājjāra āritaḥ pūrbhidāsām |

paragraphs.text: Indra, may thy terrestrial treasures reach us, and our full songs of joy approach thy dwelling.
paragraphs.original: अस्तमा ते पार्थिवा वसून्यस्मे जग्मुः सूनृता इन्द्र पूर्वीः
paragraphs.translit: astamā te pārthivā vasūnyasme jagmuḥ sūnṛtā indra pūrvīḥ
